ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Scarlet>Fire and soaring Eyes of the World
ai_show_review.blurb: The Scope show delivers a blistering Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain segue and a fierce Eyes Of The World. Jerry’s vocals and lead work are in top form, while Brent shines with a standout solo on Never Trust A Woman. Excellent soundboard recordings make this a must‑listen for ’82 fans.
ai_show_review.review:
What unfolds at The Scope captures the band riding a wave of pure '82 magic. The first set builds momentum with tight renditions of Alabama Getaway and a punchy Peggy‑O, but it’s the second set that truly ignites – the seamless Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain transition launches into an inspired Estimated Prophet → Eyes Of The World pairing, each note crackling with intensity. Brent Mydland adds texture on piano during the Estimated/Eyes outro and later delivers perhaps his best solo on Never Trust A Woman, while Phil’s bass pumps a solid groove that underpins Jerry’s soaring guitar lines and vocal inflections. The rhythm section stays locked in, driving the high‑octane Not Fade Away into a heartfelt Stella Blue before closing with a rollicking One More Saturday Night and an upbeat U.S. Blues encore.

Across the board the performance feels both exploratory and cohesive; the band’s interplay is tight yet adventurous, delivering moments that range from spacey jams to gritty rockers. The Miller soundboard capture (gd1982-04-03.142815.sbd.miller.flac2496) preserves every nuance with crystal‑clear clarity, making this show a standout entry in the 1982 catalog.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crisp cassette‑master transfer and no audible dropouts, delivering the fullest representation of the performance.

key_highlights: Scorching Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain segue that defines the second set
Fierce Eyes Of The World jam with tight bass and soaring guitar
Brent Mydland’s standout solo on Never Trust A Woman
Excellent Miller SBD capture preserving every nuance of the performance

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers powerful vocals on Scarlet and Peggy‑O, shredding lead work throughout, especially during the Scarlet>Fire segue; noted for side‑switch with Phil adding extra spark.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a deep, driving bass foundation that ‘bombs’ in the high‑energy sections; phased bass on Loser is highlighted elsewhere, reinforcing his groove throughout the show.
band_performance.Bob: Locks in solid rhythm guitar, offering stellar comping during Scarlet>Fire and keeping the jam flow tight across the set.
band_performance.Brent: Focused grand‑piano work shines on the Estimated Prophet → Eyes Of The World outro; delivers a possibly career‑best solo on Never Trust A Woman and weaves interstellar textures throughout the jams.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums stay solid, anchoring the high‑octane moments and delivering a reliable pre‑drums segment that fuels the band's momentum.
band_performance.Billy: Provides steady, driving percussion that complements Mickey’s fills, maintaining a tight rhythmic backbone through the entire performance.
